c.tagline: Ancient southern capital of dynasties, city walls, and Yangtze lore.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around 11 CNY; most locals hail via Didi. Foreign credit cards are rarely accepted, so pay by Alipay/WeChat or cash.

emergency.note: Police is 110, ambulance/medical is 120, and fire is 119. English-speaking operators are limited, so having your address in Chinese helps.

avoid.reason: Around the Confucius Temple (Fuzimiao) and other tourist areas, decline 'tea ceremony' or 'art student' invitations, which are overcharging scams.

hood_desc: Nanjing's downtown core and one of China's busiest commercial hubs, centered on the Xinjiekou traffic circle and Zifeng Tower; packed with malls, department stores, offices, and metro interchanges, it is the most convenient walkable base for first-timers.

The historic soul of Nanjing along the Qinhuai River, home to the Confucius Temple (Fuzimiao), the Imperial Examination Museum, and lantern-lit night markets; touristy but atmospheric, best for sightseeing and evening strolls by the water.

A green, relaxed district wrapped around Xuanwu Lake and the Ming-era city wall, with parks, lakeside promenades, and Jiming Temple nearby; suits travelers wanting calm scenery and open space near the center.

The forested Purple Mountain (Zhongshan) scenic area on the eastern edge of the city, holding the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, the Ming Xiaoling Tomb, and Linggu Temple; a sights-and-nature retreat of trails, gardens, and monuments.

Hexi is Nanjing's modern riverfront new town in Jianye District, built around the Youth Olympic Sports Park, the Nanjing International Expo Center, and Hexi CBD skyscrapers; orderly, spacious, and business-oriented.

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; avoid tap water and ice made from it.

transit.hours: Metro trains generally run from around 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 11:00 PM, with taxis and Didi filling the late-night gap.
transit.note: Nanjing Metro is one of China's largest systems with a dozen lines linking the airport, both high-speed rail stations, and most sights; it is the fastest and cheapest way around, backed by an extensive bus network.
transit.pay: Pay by QR code through Alipay, WeChat, or the Nanjing Metro app; a rechargeable Jinlingtong transit card and single-journey tokens are also sold at station machines. Fares are distance-based, starting around 2 CNY.

bus: Intercity coaches from Nanjing Bus Terminals to regional cities

car.idp: Required (foreign licenses not valid; a temporary Chinese permit is needed)

ferry: Yangtze River local ferry crossings (e.g. Zhongshan Wharf)
train: Nanjing South Railway Station (major high-speed rail hub)

transit.m: Metro Line S1 (Airport Line) to city center via Nanjing South (~35-45 min)
Airport coach to city center (~45-60 min)
Taxi to city center (50-60 min, ~130-150 CNY)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in Nanjing; restaurants, taxis, and cafes do not anticipate a tip, though upscale hotels may add a service charge.
